title: Cerulean Ventures - inference cost probing session
meeting_header: Date: 2025-06-23 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Redwood: Alex Chen, Priya Patel | Customer: Marta Lopez, Daniel Kim, Rita Owens, Owen Park
summary: Initial cost/unit economics discovery. Customer runs an LLM assistant and risk-scoring batch jobs; constrained budget, wants per-token cost benchmark, tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private, caching and batching levers. Agreed pilot and follow-ups: send pricing + SOC2, schedule 2-week perf run, Redwood to propose batching/cache config and estimated unit costs.
topics: per-token pricing and committed vs variable costs
hosting options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
action_items: Alex Chen - Send detailed pricing sheet (hosted per-token, reserved/dedicated pricing tiers, pilot discount) - due 2025-06-26
Priya Patel - Draft recommended batching/caching configuration for their mix (chat + rerank + batch) and expected unit-cost delta - due 2025-06-27
Rita Owens - Share SOC2 questionnaire and high-level encryption/KMS requirements with Redwood - due 2025-06-30
Daniel Kim - Provide representative traffic sample (1 week qps + sample prompts) and SLO targets - due 2025-06-26
next_steps: Redwood to email pricing + SOC2 + 'Redwood Optimize' notes
Customer to open pilot ticket and upload traffic sample
Schedule 60m benchmark kickoff for week of 2025-06-30
Security sync between Rita and Redwood security team (30m)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, I'm joined by Priya from our solutions engineering team. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Marta Lopez: Marta here, Head of ML at Cerulean.
[00:10] Daniel Kim: Daniel, platform.
[00:12] Rita Owens: Rita, security.
[00:14] Owen Park: Owen - engineering lead.
[00:16] Alex Chen: Great. High level — we wanted to understand your cost constraints, token volumes, and whether Hosted / Dedicated / Private makes sense. Priya will cover batch/cache levers later.
[00:28] Marta Lopez: Sure, top line: we run a consumer-facing finance assistant plus nightly risk scoring. Assistant is chatstyle, ~1.2M tokens/day right now, peaks at 70 qps. Risk scoring is batch jobs, about 60M tokens/day when it runs. Budget is... tight, we're targeting under $25k/mo for inference ideally.
[00:49] Priya Patel: Okay that mix helps. Do you currently have any reserved capacity or are you on pay-as-you-go with another provider?
[00:56] Marta Lopez: We're on pay-as-you-go with OpenAI for the chat and a local GPU fleet for the batch, but it's messy. Latency for chat needs to be <250ms for 95th percentile, or product will feel sluggish.
[01:11] Alex Chen: Appreciate that. Two levers we typically look at for unit cost: batching (higher throughput, lower per-token) and prefix/KV caching (if you have repeated prompts or few-shot patterns). Also model quantization or using smaller model flavors for less-critical paths.
[01:28] Daniel Kim: For risk scoring, accuracy is important but we can tolerate a slightly smaller model if quantized. For chat, accuracy matters more. Curious how Redwood handles hybrid routing — sending high-priority low-latency to dedicated nodes and batch to cheaper pools.
[01:45] Priya Patel: Yes, we support policy-based routing. You can set SLOs and traffic classes. In Hosted mode we do smart routing across instance types and model variants, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput, and Private gives you the same control plane but in your VPC/on-prem for compliance.
[02:03] Marta Lopez: Security is big for us. Rita will need SOC2 details, KMS integration, audit logs. Also data residency for EU users.
[02:12] Rita Owens: Right. We need to know retention defaults, ability to disable logs, and how keys are managed — HSM/KMS integrations. Also whether model inputs are stored for eval by default.
[02:24] Alex Chen: Short answer: Hosted has opt-in data retention and we have KMS integrations; for Private you control keys fully. We'll send SOC2 and a high-level architecture note.
[02:34] Owen Park: On batching — what's realistic for chat without adding latency? If we batch too much, we might exceed the 250ms SLO.
[02:42] Priya Patel: Right, it's a tradeoff. Continuous batching can preserve latency if you bound batch windows. E.g., with 70 qps peak we can use micro-batches at 5–10ms windows and still hit 95th of ~200–230ms depending on model. For batch risk jobs you can push throughput to maximize GPU utilization and drop per-token cost significantly.
[03:05] Marta Lopez: Can you give a ballpark per-token numbers for hosted vs dedicated? We don't need exact but directional.
[03:12] Alex Chen: Ballpark: Hosted per-token for a 32k context high-quality model might be in the mid-to-high single-digit cents per 1k tokens range depending on throughput and volume; Dedicated reserved nodes reduce that substantially, sometimes 40–60% lower for stable, high-volume workloads. But exact numbers depend on batch size, sequence length, cache hits.
[03:33] Daniel Kim: That's a wide band. Any examples where caching reduced cost?
[03:37] Priya Patel: We saw a retail assistant with lots of repeated prefix prompts — KV/prefix caching cut token cost by ~25% because the first tokens are reused from cache. For rerank workflows, sending only embeddings or smaller rerank models cut upstream tokens too.
[03:52] Marta Lopez: Our assistant has many repeated system prompts and only a few variable tokens per user — so caching seems promising.
[03:58] Priya Patel: Also consider quantized model variants for batch risk scoring. Mixed-precision or 4-bit runs can be 30–50% cheaper with small accuracy delta, especially for non-chat jobs.
[04:10] Rita Owens: From a security perspective, if we use Dedicated vs Hosted, what's the difference for data leakage risk and certifications?
[04:16] Alex Chen: Hosted has SOC2 and standard certs; data is logically isolated, with KMS integrations. Dedicated gives you physical isolation of capacity and can be contractually bounded with stricter SLAs. Private gives the highest control — you run in VPC or on-prem, customer-managed keys, full audit trail.
[04:34] Owen Park: Timeline — our VP of eng wants a recommendation in 3 weeks. Is it realistic to run a pilot and show unit economics within that window?
[04:41] Alex Chen: Yes. Typical path: 1) Redwood hosted pilot 2 weeks to measure realistic per-token at your traffic patterns (we can simulate batch and chat together), 2) analyze cached-hit rates and batching efficiency, 3) propose Dedicated reserved pools if the economics justify the committed cost.
[04:56] Marta Lopez: If we commit to Dedicated, how long are contracts and what's the ramp? We don't want a long lock-in if usage changes.
[05:03] Priya Patel: Dedicated typically has monthly or annual reserved options with the ability to configure autoscaling and burst to hosted for spikes. Contracts can be negotiated for flexibility; we can include break clauses in pilot stage.
[05:14] Daniel Kim: For the pilot, what telemetry will you need? We'll only give a sampled set of logs — can't send PII.
[05:20] Alex Chen: We only need aggregated token counts, latency histograms, sample prompts (anonymized), and ideally a 1-week qps trace. Priya will send a template.
[05:30] Owen Park: One question — model variants. Can Redwood host customer-fine-tuned models or only our selection? We have a finetuned Llama variant we prefer.
[05:39] Priya Patel: We support customer models in Private and Dedicated, and in Hosted we support uploading through our private model onboarding process with security review. For pilot it's usually easiest to use a near-equivalent open model to get baseline unit economics, then swap in your model for a follow-on run.
[05:55] Marta Lopez: Pricing: if you give us hosted numbers and a run-rate for dedicated, we can compare to our on-prem fleet costs and current OpenAI bill.
[06:02] Alex Chen: We'll send a matrix: hosted per-token tiers by monthly volume, dedicated reserved pricing by GPU type and commit level, and a simple cost model sheet that factors in caching hits and batching efficiency.
[06:12] Rita Owens: Also include retention options and whether logs are stored by default. We want to turn off retention in Hosted during pilot if possible.
[06:18] Alex Chen: Yes, opt-out retention is available. We'll document default settings and the Private path for full control.
[06:24] Daniel Kim: For batch jobs, can you separate compute for risk scoring to lower-cost quantized instances while keeping chat on low-latency nodes?
[06:31] Priya Patel: Absolutely — routing policies can pin traffic to different model flavors and node pools. That separation is key to optimizing unit cost across mixed workloads.
[06:39] Marta Lopez: What about burst capacity if we have daily peaks on chat? We can't overcommit to Dedicated for occasional spikes.
[06:45] Alex Chen: Dedicated supports autoscale with burst to hosted — that way you get predictable baseline and then temporary capacity from hosted at standard hosted rates.
[06:53] Owen Park: Any gotchas around KV cache invalidation for our agent sessions? We have short-lived sessions.
[06:58] Priya Patel: Cache TTLs are configurable per-route. For short sessions you get benefit on the system prompt and shared context across session steps; the cache hit rate depends on how repetitious the system+few-shot templates are.
[07:12] Marta Lopez: Let's talk numbers for a hypothetical: 1.2M chat tokens/day + 60M batch tokens/day => ~61.2M tokens/day. At that scale Dedicated seems worthwhile if unit goes down 50% versus hosted.
[07:27] Alex Chen: Right. We'll model both. For batch you can often push GPU to ~100% utilization and get the biggest drop in $/token; chat usually stays latency-bound so lower headroom.
[07:36] Daniel Kim: Where does Redwood Optimize fit in? We heard a bit about recommendations for quant and batching.
[07:41] Priya Patel: Redwood Optimize is our toolkit that analyzes traces and suggests batching windows, cache strategies, and model splits. For pilots we can run Optimize against your sample to give immediate levers to pull.
[07:52] Rita Owens: When you say "suggestions," does it require access to raw prompts? We need sanitized data handling.
[07:58] Priya Patel: We can run it on anonymized samples or token-level stats — not full raw PII. We also have a privacy-mode.
[08:06] Marta Lopez: Timeline check — if we agree to pilot next week, can Redwood be up in a few days?
[08:10] Alex Chen: Yes, Hosted pilot can start within 48–72 hours after we get the traffic sample and a pilot ticket. Dedicated baseline takes longer (provisioning GPUs) — usually 2–4 weeks.
[08:21] Owen Park: For cost modeling, can you show us per-token with and without caching and with small/medium/large batch sizes?
[08:28] Priya Patel: We'll produce a 3-scenario sheet: conservative (low cache hit, small batch), realistic (expected hit and mid-size batch), optimistic (high hit, large batch). Each will show $/1k tokens and monthly projection.
[08:40] Marta Lopez: Any limitations for EU data residency on Hosted? We have a subset of EU customers who must keep data in EU.
[08:46] Alex Chen: We have EU regions and can route those requests to EU-hosted capacity; Private or Dedicated in region is possible for strict residency. We'll include region-level differences in latency and cost.
[08:58] Daniel Kim: What's the quickest win to reduce our current spend? From what I'm hearing: caching + quantized batch for the nightly risk job.
[09:04] Priya Patel: That's typically the biggest delta. Move risk scoring to quantized batch instances and ensure the assistant leverages prefix caching for system tokens. Also trim unnecessary context tokens in rerank flows.
[09:15] Marta Lopez: Good. Rita, any blockers from security for a short hosted pilot?
[09:20] Rita Owens: We'll need SOC2 docs and to confirm KMS integration and retention opt-out. If those are okay, short pilot acceptable.
[09:27] Alex Chen: We'll send SOC2 + security brief. Also we'll include an NDA addendum if needed.
[09:33] Owen Park: For the pilot run, will Redwood run a synthetic replay or do we stream our live traffic?
[09:40] Priya Patel: Either works. Replay from a sample trace is common. Live traffic needs token scrubbing if it contains PII.
[09:47] Marta Lopez: We'll scrub and send a sample trace.
[09:50] Daniel Kim: Ok, last question — do you have customers that switched from on-prem to Redwood Dedicated and what were the cost outcomes?
[09:57] Alex Chen: Yes, a fintech moved risk workloads to Dedicated and saw ~45% decrease in $/token for batch jobs; chat stayed similar but benefited from latency improvements and simpler ops. We can share anonymized case study.
[10:12] Marta Lopez: That would be helpful.
[10:15] Alex Chen: Quick recap: Redwood will send pricing matrix, SOC2/security docs, Optimize notes, and a pilot plan. Customer to supply sample trace and SLOs. Next call: benchmark kickoff week of 2025-06-30.
[10:29] Rita Owens: I'll circulate the SOC2 questionnaire to Alex.
[10:32] Marta Lopez: Thanks everyone.
[10:34] Alex Chen: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:36] [call ends]
notes: Transcript shows some ASR artifacts (e.g., 'KV cash' occasionally) and speaker overlap. Customer concerned about budget ($25k/mo target) and wants pilot data before committing to Dedicated. Agreed pilot + security docs.
questions: What is the expected per-1k-token cost range for our 60M token/day batch workload in Hosted vs Dedicated?
Can Redwood run Redwood Optimize on anonymized traces to propose batching/caching settings?
What SOC2 and KMS options are available for Hosted vs Private?
